newsitem.title: GERMANY: Greenpeace dismisses EU move on novel foods.
newsitem.headline: Greenpeace dismisses EU move on novel foods.

text.p: European Union labelling plans for novel foods containing genetically modified organisms (GMOs) do not go far enough, the German branch of environmental group Greenpeace said on Thursday.

"Consumers will still be in the dark about whether the product they're buying has been in contact with biotechnology," said Joerg Naumann, leader of a campaign against genetically modified U.S. soybeans.
Greenpeace says too little is known about possible health and environmental risks from genetically altered food products, and has called for clear labelling.
But German seed processors organisation VDO in Bonn welcomed the latest plans.
Official Karl-Josef Gross said they looked as if they made the labelling of soyoil derived from such beans unnecessary.

EU states and the European Parliament agreed on Thursday to label foods containing "live" genetically modified cells and other food made from GMOs if they differed from conventional foods beyond "accepted limits of natural variation."
This ended several weeks of talks on the subject.
Naumann said, "It is unclear what scientific processes and criteria you need to prove such differences and whether they cover all eventualities."
The producer of gene-altered soybeans, U.S. chemicals firm Monsanto Co, has said soyoil derived from the new beans is identical to that from traditional beans.

Naumann said, "The EU agreement also does not specify what the labels will say. Will they have to spell out biotechnology has been used or will processors be allowed to just talk about new and improved methods?
"Consumers interested in the ethical and ecological aspects of biotechnology learn nothing about the history of a product."
He said Greenpeace would continue its campaign for the separation of gene-altered soybeans and conventional beans at source.
